name: Proxmox_VE_Ceph
description: Ceph cluster health, OSD state, placement group state and capacity for a Proxmox VE hyper-converged cluster.
technicalNotes:
Single instance, one /cluster/ceph/status call per interval, whatever the size of the Ceph cluster. Requires Sys.Audit or Datastore.Audit on /.

Verified against a real Ceph cluster on 2026-09-22. The Proxmox API declares this endpoint's return as an untyped object -- it passes through whatever `ceph status` produces -- so no field can be relied on from the schema, and Ceph has moved these keys between releases. Every field is therefore still read defensively, osdmap is accepted in both its flat and nested shapes, and each group of datapoints is withheld entirely when its source key is absent. That defensiveness is deliberate and should stay: one cluster's reply is not the schema.

Most Proxmox installs do not run Ceph. That case reports CephAvailable=0 and withholds everything else, rather than reporting a healthy cluster with zero OSDs. It is not a collection failure.

Health is three flags rather than one ordinal, because an encoding where 2 means HEALTH_ERR is something every dashboard author then has to look up. Placement group cleanliness is decided by decomposing the compound state name (active+clean, active+undersized+degraded) rather than by string-matching active+clean, so a state Ceph adds later does not silently count as clean.

datapoints.name: CephAvailable
datapoints.description: 1 when Ceph status could be read. 0 on a cluster with no Ceph configured, in which case every other datapoint here is withheld.

datapoints.name: HealthError
datapoints.alertBody: Ceph reports HEALTH_ERR. Data availability or durability is at risk; check `ceph health detail` on any node.

datapoints.name: HealthChecks
datapoints.description: Number of active Ceph health checks. The check names are written to the collection task log.

datapoints.name: OSDsOut
datapoints.description: OSDs known but not in the cluster. Expected during a planned rebalance.

datapoints.name: PGsClean
datapoints.description: Placement groups whose every state component is active or clean.

datapoints.name: PGsNotClean
datapoints.description: Placement groups in any other state: degraded, undersized, recovering, backfilling. Non-zero during normal recovery, so the threshold allows time to settle.

datapoints.name: UsedBytes
datapoints.description: Raw cluster capacity in use, bytes.

datapoints.name: UsedPercent
datapoints.description: Raw cluster utilisation. Ceph degrades badly when full, and rebalancing needs free space to work with.

datapoints.name: MonitorsInQuorum
datapoints.description: Ceph monitors currently in quorum. A cluster that loses monitor quorum is unavailable regardless of OSD state.
